download.title: Download tailored resume
download.atsNote: Output is single-column, ATS-safe (no tables, columns, or images).
download.docxFallback: {{name}} is a two-column PDF design. The Word file downloads as the single-column version — and both stay ATS-safe: no tables, text boxes or images.

standard.name: Standard
standard.desc: The default. Centred header, ruled section headings, one dense column — the plain professional CV, on US Letter.

classic.name: Classic
classic.desc: The CV Israeli recruiters expect, with every fact exactly where they look.

modern.name: Modern
modern.desc: A colour band puts your name and target role where the eye lands first.

split.name: Split
split.desc: Career story in one wide column, skills and education in a rail beside it. PDF only — the Word file downloads as the single-column version.

panel.name: Panel
panel.desc: A colour panel holds your credentials while your experience runs full height beside it. PDF only — the Word file downloads as the single-column version.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.desc: Draws your career as one continuous line — the progression reads first.

executive.name: Executive
executive.desc: Formal and understated — for finance, law and senior roles.

ivy.name: Ivy
ivy.desc: The conservative layout hiring committees in law, consulting and academia know.

ledger.name: Ledger
ledger.desc: Assertive and dense — for operators with ground to cover and numbers to show.

student.name: Student
student.desc: Built for a first or second job, where army service and projects carry the weight.

compact.name: Compact
compact.desc: Ten years of work on one page, without shrinking the type past readable.

minimal.name: Minimal
minimal.desc: Nothing but type — nothing between the reader and what you did.

changelog.flagged_other: {{count}} items may not be supported by your resume.

additions.skillsNote: Skills aren't fabrication-checked: the AI may adopt the job's wording for something you already have. Read these and drop anything you can't back up.

pages.hardOver: {{pages}} — past the {{hard}}-page ceiling. Expect it to be skimmed or dropped.

review.title: Resume review

review.empty: Nothing to fix — every check ran clean on this version.

contact-email.label: No email address
contact-email.how: Add the email address you actually read — an application system with no way to reply to you drops the CV before a person sees it.

contact-phone.label: No phone number
contact-phone.how: Add the mobile number you answer — recruiters here call before they email, and a CV they cannot phone waits.

contact-linkedin.label: No LinkedIn link
contact-linkedin.how: Paste your LinkedIn profile URL — it is the first thing a recruiter opens after the CV, and leaving it out makes them search your name and guess.

headline.label: No target-title line
headline.how: Write the job title you are applying for under your name — it is the first line a filter matches, and a real title beats no line at all.

summary-missing.label: No summary
summary-missing.how: Write two or three lines naming your field, your years of experience and the work you want next — this is what a recruiter reads before anything else.

summary-long.label: Summary runs long
summary-long.how: Cut it to about sixty words: keep your field, your strongest result and the role you are aiming at, and move everything else down into your bullets.

no-experience.label: No experience section
no-experience.how: Add at least one role, project or military position with dates and a few bullets — a CV with no experience section is filtered out before a person reads it.

dates-missing.label: Role has no dates
dates-missing.how: Add a start and an end month to this role — a reader takes a missing date for a gap you are hiding, and most parsers drop the whole entry.

dates-format.label: Dates in an odd format
dates-format.how: Write the dates as "{{suggested}}" — parsers read that form reliably and guess at everything else.

gap.label: Gap before this role
gap.how: There are {{months}} months before this role starts — account for them in one line (studies, military service, travel, freelance) so nobody has to guess.

weak-opener.label: Bullet opens weakly
weak-opener.how: Open with the action itself — built, cut, shipped, led — instead of describing what you were responsible for.

no-outcome.label: No measured result
no-outcome.how: End this bullet with the number it moved — a percentage, a time, a count of users, a sum — so a reader sees the result and not only the task.

bullet-long.label: Bullet runs long
bullet-long.how: Split it in two or cut it under twenty words — a recruiter scans the first line of a bullet and skips the rest of it.

bullet-short.label: Bullet is too short
bullet-short.how: Say what you built, what you built it with and what changed — a three-word line names a task without showing you did it.

repeated-verb.label: Same opener repeated
repeated-verb.how: "{{verb}}" opens three or more of your bullets — vary the repeats so the list reads as separate pieces of work rather than one long job.

duplicate-bullet.label: Two bullets say the same thing
duplicate-bullet.how: Keep the stronger one and delete this, or make it specific to this role — a repeat spends a line and adds no new claim.

buzzword.label: Filler phrase
buzzword.how: Delete the phrase and put the evidence in its place — write the thing you did that would make a reader say it about you.

pronoun.label: Written in first person
pronoun.how: Drop the "I" and "my" and start on the verb — CV bullets are written without pronouns, and the reader already knows the page is about you.

acronym.label: Acronym never spelled out
acronym.how: Write it once as {{pair}} and use the short form after that — a keyword filter searches for one spelling and your CV carries only the other.

entry-empty.label: Role with no bullets
entry-empty.how: Add two or three bullets saying what you built and what changed — a title and dates prove you held the job, not that you did anything in it.

edu-placeholder.label: Template text instead of a school
edu-placeholder.how: Replace it with the real institution name — this text came from a template and it is printing on your CV as though it were where you studied.

duplicate-entry.label: Credential printed twice
duplicate-entry.how: Delete the second copy — the same degree or certificate listed twice reads as padding rather than as two qualifications.

skills-few.label: Very few skills listed
skills-few.how: List at least ten tools, languages and platforms you genuinely work with — a filter matches this section first, and a short list scores low against every job.

skills-sentence.label: Skill written as a sentence
skills-sentence.how: Cut it to the term itself — "PostgreSQL", not a sentence about it — so a filter can match it and the chip fits on one line.

skills-unasked.label: Mostly skills this job never asks for
skills-unasked.how: Lead with the tools the posting actually names and move the rest down or off — this section is read as a shortlist for one job, not as an inventory.

length.label: Length does not match the experience
length.how: This renders as {{pages}} pages against {{years}} years of experience — aim for one page up to about ten years and two beyond that, trimming the oldest roles and the weakest bullets first.

file.note: Rendered by the same call the Download button makes, from your resume exactly as it stands — every change you have accepted or declined included.
file.failed: Couldn't build the PDF just now.
file.morePages_one: 1 more page is in the download.
file.morePages_other: {{count}} more pages are in the download.

ats.note: We render that PDF, then read it back with the same parser we run on resumes people upload. What follows is the file's own text — not a text version of the page above.
ats.failed: Couldn't read the file back just now.

screen.note: This page is drawn in the template you picked — its colours, headings, header, entry layout and bullets. What it can't copy is the typeface: the file carries its own, so you get the same serif or sans here, not the exact letters.
screen.icons: This one also draws small marks beside your contact details in the PDF; the page above leaves them out.
screen.twoColumn: This template also prints as two columns, with a rail beside the main story. Which sections land in that rail is decided while the file is built, so the page above shows one column rather than guessing wrong.
screen.footer: It also prints your name at the foot of every page of the PDF, so a second page still says whose it is. The page above is one continuous sheet with no page breaks to foot, and the Word file leaves it out.

replace.title: Replace your resume
replace.body: Upload a new file and it becomes your master resume everywhere — this page, job matching, interview prep and every tool.

overlay.replaces: This starts again from your master resume. The review on screen is replaced; your saved master is not changed.
overlay.replacesEdited_one: This starts again from your master resume — and deletes the 1 line you typed onto this CV. It did not reach your tracker, so there is no way to get it back. Your saved master is not changed either way.
overlay.replacesEdited_other: This starts again from your master resume — and deletes the {{count}} lines you typed onto this CV. They did not reach your tracker, so there is no way to get them back. Your saved master is not changed either way.
overlay.replacesSaved_one: This starts again from your master resume and replaces the draft saved with this job, with the 1 line you typed. Your saved master is not changed.
overlay.replacesSaved_other: This starts again from your master resume and replaces the draft saved with this job, with the {{count}} lines you typed. Your saved master is not changed.
overlay.replacesKept: This starts again from your master resume. The draft on screen stays saved with its job in your tracker, and your saved master is not changed.
overlay.title: Tailor for a job
overlay.hint: Paste the posting, or drop in its link and we'll fetch it.
overlay.failed: Couldn't read that posting just now.
overlay.topMissing: Most-wanted terms your CV doesn't say yet
overlay.topPartial: Close — but not in the posting's own words

discard.title: Close this review and edit your master resume again
discard.edited_one: Leaving takes the 1 line you typed onto this CV with it. Your master resume is unchanged either way.
discard.edited_other: Leaving takes the {{count}} lines you typed onto this CV with it. Your master resume is unchanged either way.

fit.title: How this CV matches the job
fit.coverageNote: Recomputed from your CV as it stands right now — every change you accept or decline, and every word you type in yourself, is already in this number.
fit.asOf: One AI reading, taken {{time}}. It doesn't move as you edit: a second reading costs another model call, and part of any difference between two readings is sampling noise rather than progress.
fit.notMeasuredNote: Reading how a recruiter would rate this costs one model call. Check fit, or tailor, and it appears here.

edit.hint: Tap anything on your resume to edit it.
edit.tailoredHint: Type anywhere to change this application's CV. Your master resume is untouched.
edit.tailoredNoAdd: To add something new, edit your master resume and tailor again.
edit.tailoredNoBlankEntry: Emptying every field would leave a blank entry on the CV, not remove it — and it would print that way. To take a whole role, project, degree or service out, edit your master resume and tailor again.
edit.yoursRestoreCleared_one: Put back the 1 edit I cleared
edit.yoursRestoreCleared_other: Put back the {{count}} edits I cleared
edit.local: Changes are on this device until you save.
edit.saveErrorFallback: Couldn't save your resume. Your changes are still here — try again.
edit.langWarnTitle: This would save over your other resume
edit.langWarnBody: Your resume is stored one per language. These edits now read as {{lang}}, so saving would replace your {{lang}} resume and leave this one unchanged.
edit.gone: That part of your resume is no longer there.
